title: Independent sets are complements of vertex coverings
statement: Let $G$ be a graph with vertex set $V$, and let $S \subseteq V$. Then $S$ is an independent set of $G$ — no edge of $G$ has both of its ends in $S$ — if and only if the complement $V \setminus S$ is a covering of $G$, that is, every edge of $G$ has at least one end in $V \setminus S$.
hypotheses_covered: S is a subset of the vertex set V
replaced:
A set $S \subseteq V$ is an independent set of $G$ if and only
if $V \backslash S$ is a covering of $G$.
